_comment: Committed baseline for the search-relevance golden set. Regenerate deliberately and review the diff — never re-baseline to make a red build green. Metrics are measured over the frozen fixtures in ./fixtures and ./fixtures-web, so they only move when the ranker moves.
_lastMoveComment: 2026-08-01, query understanding (modifier inflection + romance translation). coverage 0.902 -> 1.0: the 5 queries that returned nothing from any chain now return something. precisionAt5 0.991 -> 0.98 and mrr 1.0 -> 0.987 in the same change, and that is NOT a ranking regression — those two are means over *answered* queries only, so they were previously an average of the 46 easiest. End to end (every query counted, empty scored 0) went 0.894 -> 0.98 and 0.902 -> 0.987. Verified per query before re-baselining: no individual query's P@5 fell, 5 rose from 0. Only the 13 fixtures the change can affect were re-captured; the other 38 stay frozen so vendor drift is not in the same diff.
_tiersComment: vendor = raw 7-chain fan-out. web = the same fan-out plus web-search augmentation, which injects web-discovered products at the HEAD of the merged list and so can put a product in the top 5 that the vendor tier never saw. Both are gated; the local SQLite catalog is excluded from both because its contents are environment-specific and would make fixtures irreproducible.
_metricsComment: precisionAt5/mrr measure RANKING over queries that returned something. coverage is the answer rate and is gated separately: a query-understanding change that stops matching a hard class of queries would otherwise raise the ranking metrics by removing those queries from the average.
_knownGateViolationsComment: Empty on purpose in both tiers. The two defects this corpus was built around — Milchdrink UHT returning Milchschokolade, and Protein Milch returning bread — do NOT reproduce in either tier against the 2026-08-01 capture. They are not known to be fixed (matcher.ts last changed 2026-06-19, six weeks before they were reported), so the gate queries stay armed as regression guards rather than being recorded as accepted breakage.
_webTierComment: No web-tier fixtures are committed. Augmentation could not be captured honestly from this machine: the auto chain is ddg-html -> ddg-lite -> google-cse, and here both DDG endpoints return an HTTP 202 bot challenge while google CSE returns a permanent 400. The paid providers whose keys are configured are deliberately NOT in the auto chain (decided 2026-07-25 — DDG works through the deployed egress). A capture attempted anyway produced pools identical to the vendor tier for 49 of 51 queries, i.e. coverage in name only, so it was discarded rather than committed. Re-run `npm run eval:capture -- --web` from an egress DDG serves.
